shouldFix.title: The repair history twice calls the rejected non-object payload a CC-5 member without attributing that label to v3's misclassification
shouldFix.claimUnderReview: v6 says it lands G21FXV5-S1 while preserving the rule that non-object top level is RF-2 but not CC-5. Its purpose and v3 finding disposition nevertheless describe v4 as removing 'the non-object-top-level CC-5 member'.
primaryEvidence: $.purpose says v4 performed 'catalog removal of the non-object-top-level CC-5 member'. $.appliesFindingsOf.v3[0].landed repeats 'catalog removal of the non-object-top-level CC-5 member'. Neither occurrence says 'the entry v3 labeled CC-5', 'the purported CC-5 member', or 'the member v3 misclassified as CC-5'.

The closed c50a79fe... contract puts non-object top level in RF-2 covers and omits it from $.hostileDualChannelConformance.classes[4].intent. v6 correctly restates that rule at $.controlFrameEncoding.cc5ClassificationRule: 'non-object top level is in RF-2 covers and is absent from the closed CC-5 intent.'

The corrected remainder note at $.whatIsNotAuthored[17] demonstrates the required precision: 'rejected v3 RF-2 non-object-top-level payload; not a CC-5 member'. Calling the same payload a 'CC-5 member' on the repair-history surface is inconsistent unless the invalid v3 label is expressly attributed.

$.failsIf[6] says the artifact fails if non-object top level is classified as CC-5, while $.doesNot[16] disclaims that classification. The two unqualified noun phrases reproduce the forbidden classification even though their historical context makes clear that removal, not future authoring, is intended.

The v5 chronology repair itself is otherwise present and accurate: v4 performed the active-catalog removal, v5 repaired the remainder classification, and v6 pins v5 as Split with Codex REJECT 0/1 G21FXV5-S1.
shouldFix.impact: The active v6 catalog, current remainder inventory, and future-work scope all correctly exclude non-object top level from CC-5, so this wording does not presently authorize bytes or reopen the class remainder. It does put the rejected class label back into the artifact's purpose and authoritative findings ledger without marking it as v3's invalid label, directly on the lineage surface whose job is to explain the repair. That creates an avoidable contradiction with the closed class rule and the artifact's own failsIf. Because the current fixture and remainder semantics are sound and the defect is attribution in repair history, it is SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX.
shouldFix.requiredRemedy: In a successor, replace both instances of 'the non-object-top-level CC-5 member' with unambiguous attributed language such as 'the non-object-top-level catalog entry that v3 misclassified as CC-5'. Preserve the now-correct chronology: v4 removed the active catalog entry, v5 completed G21FXV3-M1 by repairing the remainder and thereby landed G21FXV4-M1, and v6's successor lands G21FXV5-S1. Keep v3, v4, and v5 frozen and Split; preserve the two current fixture byte sequences, open leftover-design, and all no-execution/no-SATISFIED boundaries.

decision: REJECT — 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX. Custody passes: the subject remains 65134cb9... mode 0444; the fixtures remain df3f6198... and 76cc5805... mode 0444; all 31 cited path/digest occurrences reproduce; v3, v4, and v5 are accurately pinned as Split; HEAD and last heading remain D-244; required-now remains 28; protected files are unchanged; G21 was not executed. v6 substantively lands G21FXV5-S1 by distinguishing v4's catalog removal from v5's remainder-inventory completion. Replace both with attributed misclassification language.
